message.content:
**How to kill Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate a running program with the `taskkill` utility.  
Below are the most common ways to stop VS Code (and its helper processes) safely.

---

### 1. Kill by image name (recommended)

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Kill by **image name** – works even if the process has been renamed or started under a different user. |
| `/F`   | Force termination (equivalent to “End Task”). |
| `/T`   | Terminate the specified process **and any child processes** it spawned (e.g., renderer, extensions). |

> **Why `/T`?**  
> VS Code spawns several helper processes (`code.exe`, `code.exe (renderer)`, etc.). Using `/T` ensures all of them are closed, preventing orphaned background tasks.

---

### 2. Kill by Process ID (PID)

If you prefer to target a specific instance:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

This lists all `code.exe` instances with their PIDs. Then:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
```

Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the actual number shown.

---

### 3. Quick one‑liner (all instances)

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

Runs in a single command; no need to look up PIDs manually.

---

### 4. Using PowerShell (alternative)

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

PowerShell’s `Stop-Process` is essentially a wrapper around `taskkill`. It’s handy if you’re already in a PowerShell session.

---

## Practical Tips

| Tip | Explanation |
|-----|-------------|
| **Use `/F` only when necessary** | If VS Code is responding, you can omit `/F` to allow a graceful shutdown. |
| **Avoid killing unrelated `code.exe`** | If you have multiple users or remote sessions, double‑check the PID or use `/FI "USERNAME eq <your_user>"`. |
| **Automate with a batch file** | Create `kill-vscode.bat` containing `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` and run it whenever you need to force close. |
| **Check for orphaned processes** | After killing, run `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` again to confirm all instances are gone. |

---

### Example Session

```cmd
C:\> tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ ========= ============
code.exe                    12345 Console                    1     150,000 K
code.exe                    67890 Console                    1     120,000 K

C:\> taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
SUCCESS: Sent termination signal to process "code.exe" (PID 12345).
SUCCESS: Sent termination signal to process "code.exe" (PID 67890).

C:\> tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
INFO: No tasks are running which match the specified criteria.
```

That’s it! You’ve successfully terminated VS Code and all its child processes using `taskkill`.
